displayName: onV2AnswerCreated is discarding cohort counts at the breakdown cap

documentation.content:
The aggregate trigger is acting at the breakdown cap: a question has answers from more distinct values of one anchor than `BREAKDOWN_MAX_BUCKETS` (24) can hold, and the cells the hot document cannot hold are going to its tail (`v2_agg_overflow/{qid}-{shard}`, D400).

What fires this: `foldAnchors` / `foldCanonAnchors` (functions/src/pure.ts) report through a callback whenever the cap acts, and the trigger logs `metric: agg_evict` at WARNING after the transaction commits (`logBucketCaps`, functions/src/v2.ts) — one line per discard. `kind` says which of the two things happened: `evicted` means a bucket holding fewer than `BUCKET_EVICT_BELOW` (5) answers was dropped, count and all, to admit a newcomer; `refused` means every slot is published and the newcomer went to the tail instead. Since D400 NEITHER discards on the vote path — the evicted cell moves whole, the refused newcomer starts in the tail, and hot ∪ tail is exact — so this alert no longer means lost counts; it means the tail is live for that question, and every reader whose city or country is in it pays one shard read per such question at the City or Country stop. `dim` and `bucket` name the value.

Why this is a separate policy from the error and contention alerts: the answer folds and the transaction commits. Nothing throws, nothing retries, and the hot document is complete only together with its tail. No other signal sees the cap act.

What it means. City (~11k values) and country (249) are the only dimensions that can reach the cap; the others are closed vocabularies far under it. At launch scale this is dormant. Sustained firing on one question means that question is being answered from more places than the document holds, and the City stop is quietly a fact about the 24 biggest places. A burst of `evicted` lines with `total: 1` on values nobody recognises is the other reading — a junk-value burst against the cap, the attack the eviction rule exists to absorb — and the log line's `bucket` tells the two apart.

First response: read the lines — `gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.metric="agg_evict"' --limit 50 --project prvfire33` — and note which qid, which dim and which kind. A `refused` burst on one daily question is the expected shape at scale and needs nothing but a number moved: `B.tailShare` in scripts/cost-arith.mjs is 0 until this fires, and the share of answers landing in the tail is what it should become (COSTS.md's row). An `evicted` burst with `total: 1` on values nobody recognises is a junk-value burst against the cap — the eviction rule absorbing it, as designed, with the junk now parked in the tail rather than blanking the dimension. Raise the threshold only once the tail is the ordinary state of the daily questions; until then the first fire is worth reading.

Not urgent: no count is lost anywhere on the vote path, and `npm run rebuild:agg` (functions/src/replay.ts) rebuilds a question's hot document and all eight tail shards from its answers, exactly. The catalog fold takes no tail (its published `by` is a lossy projection by design, D17), so a line whose qid is a catalogue pick still means a discarded cell there.
